{"candidate_rtl":"module decoder_8bit\n #(\n    parameter N = 8\n) (\n    input [N-1:0] in,\n    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out\n);\n    always @(*) begin\n        out = {(1<<N){1'b0}};\n        out[in] = 1'b1;\n    end\nendmodule","bottleneck":"The output is a one-hot decode of all input bits; the critical path is the shared input buffering and multi-level decode logic feeding the selected output bit.","rewrite":"Replace the variable-width shift expression with an explicit zero-initialize plus variable bit-select assignment. This directly expresses a one-hot decoder and allows synthesis to balance and factor the decode logic without changing the 256-bit output behavior.","expected_timing_gain":"Likely neutral to modest improvement over the baseline, approximately 0% to 10%, depending on ABC factoring and buffering decisions.","area_or_other_cost":"Expected area is approximately equal to or slightly below the baseline because the explicit decoder form avoids any shift-operator interpretation overhead. No additional state, storage, or external logic is introduced.","functional_boundaries":"For every binary value of in, exactly one output bit is 1 at index in and all other output bits are 0.
